title: Gravity and Protocol
premise: Lior Pemberton, a xenolinguist exiled to the forgotten colony of Meridian-9 after refusing to weaponize their translations, records the colony's slow abandonment while losing the ability to dream in any human language. When a distress signal arrives in Ashkari — a language extinct for two centuries that Lior alone can still read — they discover the war's supposed enemy has been begging for peace for years, silenced by those who profit from the conflict. Pursued by the military intelligence officer who once destroyed their career, Lior must smuggle the message through collapsing colony infrastructure and their own deteriorating sense of self. In the end, Lior broadcasts the truth at the cost of their exile's safety, choosing belonging with the colonists over invisibility, and the ceasefire holds — though not everyone who helped them survives.
about_author: Ansel Blackwood is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent a decade documenting dying languages before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the fog, they insist, sounds different every morning.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. On decaying Meridian-9, Lior records the colony's final months in a private audio log, translating bureaucratic evacuation notices no one reads. They dream in fragments of dead languages now, never human ones. Emotional beat: quiet grief and self-imposed isolation, establishing what Lior has lost and why they chose to disappear.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A routine sweep of derelict relay stations catches a repeating transmission in Ashkari, extinct since the Ashkar Purges two centuries ago. Lior translates the first lines alone at night: it is a plea for ceasefire, timestamped years ago. Emotional beat: electrified dread — being needed is the thing Lior fled.

chapters.title: What the Colony Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Sefa Okonjo, the colony's stubborn administrator. Lior hesitantly shares fragments; Sefa reveals Meridian-9 was itself a dumping ground for inconvenient people. The colonists decide, informally, to help. Emotional beat: first fragile threads of belonging, offered by people with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Knew Their Name
chapters.summary: Intelligence officer Captain Veyra Sol's POV. Veyra arrives on Meridian-9 hunting an unregistered transmission, carrying Lior's old file — and old guilt. She interviews colonists with surgical courtesy. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Veyra is both threat and mirror, someone else shaped by the machine she serves.

chapters.title: Grammar of the Enemy
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Decoding deepens: the message proves the 'enemy' species learned Ashkari as a peace gesture generations ago, and the war's continuation depends on that never being known. Lior realizes their own past refusal made them the last person alive who could read it. Emotional beat: purpose rekindling into obsession, dreams turning fully nonhuman.

chapters.title: Evacuation Order
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Command declares Meridian-9 condemned; forced removal begins in ten days. Veyra uses the chaos to search openly, and a young colonist, Tam, is detained on suspicion of aiding Lior. Emotional beat: the cost of caring crystallizes — invisibility protected no one but Lior.

chapters.title: The Relay Graveyard
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. To broadcast planet-wide, Lior must physically reach the ancient relay array across the ash flats, guided by Sefa while Veyra closes in. A storm strands them; in a shelter, Lior finally tells Sefa the whole truth of their disgrace. Emotional beat: confession as intimacy; trust forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Veyra confronts Lior privately — not with arrest, but with an offer: hand over the translation and be restored, reinstated, remembered. Lior refuses, and Veyra, shaken, lets them go long enough to doubt her orders. Emotional beat: the antagonist's crisis; justice versus loyalty inside the law.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, climax. At the relay array, with Veyra's forces descending, Lior transmits the full Ashkari message in both tongues — and adds their own testimony. Tam, freed by sympathetic soldiers, opens the jamming grid from inside. Veyra stands down rather than fire. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into voice; Lior speaks, finally, as themselves.

chapters.title: A Language Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, resolution. Ceasefire talks begin; the colonists choose to stay and rebuild rather than scatter. Lior, no longer exiled but no longer invisible, begins teaching Ashkari to the colony's children — and dreams, one night, in a human voice again. Emotional beat: belonging earned, identity reconciled, hope without sentimentality.
